label: paragraph_title
text: TYPHOON DAMAGE.

label: paragraph_title
text: IMPORTANT SUPREME COURT ACTION.

label: text
text: HON. MR. H. W. BIRD'S EVIDENCE.

label: text
text: The Hon. Mr. H. W. Bird was crossed-examined this morning in connection with a Supreme Court action for the setting aside of an award made by him as arbitrator in connection with houses built in Kennedy Road and which were damaged by a landslide caused by the typhoon of 1923.

label: text
text: The case for the plaintiff is that under an agreement the contractor who erected the houses to plaintiff's order was liable for any such damage and had no right to claim, extra in respect of it. Mr. Bird, in his award, had found for the contractor.

label: text
text: Mr. F. C. Jenkin, counsel for the plaintiff, asked Mr. Bird if he had not put the following question to the plaintiff when the arbitration proceedings were proceeding: "If the damage to a contractor through typhoon damage was something like $200,000 would you still expect him to shoulder the loss?"

label: text
text: Mr. Bird: Something to that effect.

label: text
text: Mr. Jenkin: And your reply to that was "Oh, no, you cannot break a man like that."

label: text
text: Mr. Bird: Something like that.

label: text
text: Mr. Jenkin: It would be in your mind that it was an unjust thing to penalise a contractor where the damage was very large and that therefore it was not when the damage was small. Must you not keep to the principle in adjudicating on these matters?

label: text
text: Mr. Bird: I tried to bring the matter home to him.

label: text
text: Mr. Jenkin further suggested in the course of cross-examination that Mr. Bird showed great haste and impatience with the plaintiff in the course of the arbitration because of the insistence with which he struck to his ground that "according to contract he should not be saddled with such a large sum of money."

label: text
text: Mr. Bird replied that he had shown no undue haste but that he had made it quite clear to the plaintiff that it was no use arguing that particular point as he had already made up his mind about it.

label: text
text: Asked why he did not at the time of the interview look at the particular clause in the agreement referred to by the plaintiff Mr. Bird said that he was already fully conversant with it.

label: text
text: In a declaration sworn to quite recently by Mr. Bird, said Mr. Jenkin, Mr. Bird had corrected a statement made previously that only one party had been present at the hearing and had amended it so that it read both were present. The statement was not even yet clear, said Mr. Jenkin, for it would be a fair reading of the amended statement to infer that both had given evidence.

label: text
text:
Mr. Bird: Both were present but Lam. Tuk (the contractor) was not called upon to say anything. Why I did not say so in the first statement I cannot remember. It was over a year ago.
In the course of evidence Mr. Bird had stated that there was no need for Lam Tuk to be called upon as his case was simply the presenting of a bill of extras.

label: paragraph_title
text: Earlier Evidence.

label: text
text: The case Wils' closed yesterday afternoon of the plaintiff in a Supreme Court action respecting an award made by the Hon. Mr. H. W. Bird as arbitrator.

label: text
text: In his final argument for the man who had let out a contract for the building of two houses in Kennedy Rond, Mr. F. U. Jenkin said that the arbitrator's award was most improper and unreasonable enough to amount to a miscarriage of justice. Mr. Bird had found that the contractor was entitled to claim extras from plaintiff in respect of typhoon damage whilst the houses were in course of construction and had refused to look at the contract between the two parties.

label: text
text: The plaintiff, said counsel, had no idea that the arbitration proceedings had concluded when it appeared later that they had done. Seven weeks of silence had followed certain earlier proceedings and had the plaintiff known that a summons to the office of Messrs. Palmer and Turner with which they were followed, was looked upon as final he would have asked permission to call upon the services of a lawyer. Had he consulted one the advice would have been given him to call on the arbitrator to state a special case to place before a court.

label: text
text: FINANCIAL DEPRESSION.

label: text
text: Seen by a “China Mall” reporter this morning, a leading stockbroker said that there was little to be done in Ice House Street where the accumulated business had still to be cleared up.

label: text
text: “Even nominally,” he admitted, “arrears had not been made good and the only thing to do was to wait for a return to normal times. Financially, the position was no better off than when the trouble began although in other directions there had been vast improvement.”

label: text
text: "Money cannot be got out of the ground," the speaker replied to a query, "not even on gift-edged security."

label: paragraph_title
text: VALLEY FLOOD.

label: text
text: STEAM ROLLER WATCH MAN'S DEATH INQUIRY.

label: text
text: Sitting us Coroner at the Central Magistracy yesterday, and assisted by a jury composed of Messrs. D. 'Temperley (foeman), A. D. Russell and C. J. Joseph, Mr. S. B. B. McElderry conducted an inquiry into the circumstances attending the death of a P.W.D. coolie named Tong Fat, who was guiding a P.W.D. steam roller, during the recent floods at Happy Valley.

label: text
text: Mr. St. W. Lo appeared on behalf of the directors of the Young Wo Nursing Home, and Mr. E. F. C. Brooks watched proceedings on behalf of Dr. Leung Cheung-man.

label: text
text: The Coroner said that the man was killed by the collapse of a wall, and there was therefore the question of responsibility. He asked the solicitors to refrain from asking questions which were not concerned with the proceedings as a death inquiry.

label: text
text: Dr. E. P. Minnett deposed to having conducted a post mortem examination on June 17, on the body of a cookie identified as Tong Rat. The ribs on the right side were broken and the liver and spleen were ruptured. Witness considered that death must have been instantaneous.

label: text
text: A Chinese constable said that at 1:30 a.m. on June 16, he received

label: text
text: a report that a ten-shed had been washed away by the flood. On arriving at the scene the found a man lying dead across the nullah on the rice course. The body was lying in water, and the arms were pinioned with stones. Another body was found half an hour later. Both the bodies were taken to the mortuary where they were identified.

label: text
text: Dr. Clau Wai-cheng, managing director of the Yeung Wo Nursing Home, gave evidence describing the state in which he found the Home on the night of the flood.

label: text
text: The next witness was Lo Shumchi, foreman for the Tung San contractors, owners of the site. After a series of questions put to this witness by the foreman of the jury and the Coroner, it was elicited that he was in charge of the building of the wall on a plan prepared by Mr. Raven. His instructions were to construct the wall with one part of cement and six parts of sand, the latter being taken from the hillside. There were also bands of cement concrete running through the wall, the concrete being composed of one part cement, three parts sand, and six parts stone. The wall was 20 feet above the level of the ground with a base of nine feet. Witness stated that the construction of the wall commenced in January and the work was finished three days before the acid化, but there had not been enough time for the mortar to settle down.

label: text
text: A report on the site was submitted by Mr. Boothby, engineer of the Kowloon-Canton Railway, and Mr. H. A. Goldsmith, engineer in charge of roads, P.W.D., gave evidence as to drainage on Stubbs Road.

label: text
text: The inquiry was adjourned until this afternoon.

label: paragraph_title
text: CONTRADICTORY.

label: text
text:
CHARGE AGAINST A COOLIE
DISMISSED.

label: text
text: A coolie was charged at the Kowloon Magistracy this morning with depositing night soil at the back of Aimai Villas.

label: text
text: The complainant, Mr. E. C. Bell, a special constable, deposed to having seen the accused emptying a bucket into a surface gutter.

label: text
text: The accused denied the complaint's story.

label: text
text: Mrs. King, of No. 2, Aimai Villas, stated in evidence that she saw the accused, after cleaning her bathroom, put the night soil into the servants' lavatory and not into the gutter.

label: text
text: Other evidence was also tendered, which all went in favour of the accused.

label: text
text: His Worship said that he could not convict on evidence which was contradictory, and discharged the accused.

label: text
text: BANK HOLIDAY MATCHES.

label: text
text: After the August Bank Holiday the counties have generally sorted themselves out in the Home cricket season.

label: text
text: Results which came in this morning show that Yorkshire (the champions) and Surrey (who are second) were both checked. However, they retain their respective places in the table, although Lancashire are only a fraction behind Surrey.

label: text
text: It will be seen that J. B. Hobbs has still to make that century to tie the record standing in the name of Dr. W. G. Grace, namely, 126 centuries in first-class cricket. The Oval record crowd mentioned by Reuter must have been sorely disappointed when their favourite failed and when Notts robbed the home side of four points.

label: text
text: Even if Lancashire do not bear out the prediction of "Plum" Warner that they will win the championship, they will have the satisfaction of knowing that they made their traditional rivals, Yorkshire, drop eight points in the two matches. No other team has deprived the White Rose of more than two points. However, Yorkshire seem assured of the top place as they have only one more stiff match, that with Surrey at the Oval, commencing this Saturday. Surrey won the corresponding match last year and it is to be hoped that Sadler, the Surrey fast bowler, will rout the Northerners again if only to keep
